claims.statement: NFZ publishes central validation and verification rules that can expressly make a reported service ineligible for settlement when authorization or required conditions are missing.
Published NFZ checks include cases where a service cannot be settled because a prerequisite hospitalization, service, interval, or frequency condition was not reported or met.

contrary_evidence: Hospital and clinic information-system vendors may already encode many NFZ checks.
Published rules do not reveal the actual preventable rejection volume or willingness to switch tools.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: one billing outsourcer can introduce ten providers using the same specialty workflow.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 350 providers at 1500 PLN monthly would produce 6.3 million PLN ARR; secure, low-churn infrastructure could support founder net worth above 5 million PLN in years 6 to 10.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 20 hours weekly for one specialty, with privacy, security, and NFZ billing experts retained.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 70% gross margin after secure support and rule maintenance.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: a 15000 PLN connector and channel build repays within ten provider-months at 70% contribution margin.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 1500 PLN per provider-month for one specialty contract, with connector setup billed separately.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Hypothesis: monthly settlement and rule changes create durable repeat use if accuracy is demonstrable.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A de-identified rule-to-correction taxonomy and specialty-specific dependency graph without pooling patient records
fingerprint.customer: Independent Polish rehabilitation or home-care providers and outsourced NFZ billing teams
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Medical billing outsourcers, specialty associations, clinic-accounting firms, and HIS resellers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Local-first reimbursement rules engine with paid connector and rule-update subscriptions
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The provider pays monthly for each contract whose claim batch receives a versioned preflight report
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A monthly service batch is ready for NFZ submission and payment eligibility must be checked

founder_fit: The founder combines healthcare literacy, data science, and access to a medical-student perspective.
A rules and anomaly engine is technically aligned and can run locally.
Billing outsourcers and clinic-software partners provide non-personal-brand distribution.
risks: Health-data processing creates high security and GDPR obligations.
Rule lag could create false confidence or missed reimbursement.
Sales into healthcare may require more meetings and support than the founder prefers.

structure.control_point: Versioned claim-batch pass before NFZ submission
structure.critical_dependency: Current rule interpretation, secure local integration, and measurable preventable denials

thesis: A local-first preflight engine for independent rehabilitation and home-care providers could compile published NFZ validation logic into a human-readable claim graph, test a batch before submission, and preserve the rule version and correction decision behind each pass. The first product would process pseudonymized or on-premise exports and never need patient data in a shared training corpus.
title: NFZ Claim Preflight for Rehabilitation Providers
uncertainties: A narrow specialty with enough rejected value and weak incumbent tooling must be identified.
The permitted export and integration patterns differ across clinic systems.
The 85000 PLN capital figure and all pricing or scale figures below are hypotheses.
